article.headline: Intuitive Machines Rises 7.0% After Record Quarter, Backlog Reaches $1.9 Billion
article.deck: A fast-growing space business with a broken chart: the close sits 72.2% below the 46.85 buy point of a 23-week deep cup.
body: Intuitive Machines sells the trip to space and the moon. It delivers satellites, science instruments and cargo to destinations in space, including the lunar surface, offers rideshare delivery, collects and processes space-based data, and provides infrastructure services for navigation. It is a small company by market value, about $2.10 billion, carrying a backlog that its chief executive put at $1.9 billion.

The stock rose 0.85 to 13.03 today, up 7.0%, on volume 3.53x its 50-day average, as the company reported its third quarter. Stocktwits carried the CEO calling the quarter a record, with revenue of $269 million. 24/7 Wall St. reported the stock surged 16% on the record quarter and positive free cash flow, and Proactive had it up 14% as revenue and backlog beat expectations. By the close the gain was 7.0%; after hours it traded at 13.15, up 0.9%.

The case is revenue. The latest quarter in the desk's table, June, brought in $203.4 million, up 304.3% from a year earlier. The four quarters given run $51.0 million, $43.3 million, $183.6 million and $203.4 million. The company is not yet profitable: EPS was a loss of 0.29 a share in June, after losses of 0.06, 0.33 and 0.25 in the three quarters before it. Barron's summed up the day as the stock heading back to the moon as revenues rise.

What the market is paying: about $2.10 billion in market value and a forward P/E of -65.15, which means there are no forward earnings to put a multiple on. Investors are paying for the backlog and the sales line.

The chart is the hard part. The stock sits in a 23-week deep cup that fell 82.4% from its May 28 high to a Nov. 5 low. The buy point is 46.85, and the close is 72.2% below it. The 52-week range runs from 7.78 to 46.75. Today's close sits 0.6% above the 50-day line at 12.95 and 32.6% below the 200-day at 19.34; the session's low held 1.26 ATRs above the 21-day line at 11.52.

The stock is up 18.2% in a month but down 31.5% over three months and down 19.7% this year; over one year it is up 38.0%. It ranks 81 of 99 on the desk's list, but its RS line is 71.6% below its high. The desk's 50-day bounce entry at 14.71 is not live.
This is a growing business with a chart that needs months of repair. The quarter moved the stock back above its 50-day line; the base still has most of an 82.4% decline to rebuild.
article.watch: Whether the stock holds the 50-day line at 12.95 now that the quarter is out.

chief.verdict: The tape is in a correction and the leaders' charts say so: the Nasdaq sits 3.8% under its 50-day and 8.5% off its high, and almost everything in a buy range got there on thin breakouts or weak earnings. The few clean setups are outside tech's mainstream, in energy and defensive names like EOG and COST, while the strongest growth names (ANET, AMD at RS 99) are still building bases rather than breaking out. Risk leans down; the Dow just logged another distribution day on 1.85 times average volume.
chief.market: With 5 distribution days on the S&P 500 (weighted 5.5) and 5 on the Nasdaq (weighted 6.5) and the market in correction, keep exposure light, one or two small starter positions at most and mostly cash.

picks.why: The cleanest chart on the desk: a 4-week flat base only 10.9% deep, the stock 0.9% over the pivot, 3.9% above the 50-day and just 0.1 ATR stretched, with earnings already out (EPS up 97.4% in the September quarter) and a forward P/E near 9.3. The risk is the breakout itself: it came on 0.82 times average volume, and the RS line sits 13.3% under its high, so this is an oil trade as much as a leader.
